title: Place
description: A place that can be named and returned to — a library, a hall, a park, a street address, a point on the ground. Modelled on schema.org/Place, which is the widest-shared vocabulary for this and which solves nesting with ONE self-referential type rather than two: a room inside a building is a Place whose `containedInPlace` is the building. That is why there is no separate address or location type here. An address has no identity apart from the thing it locates — nobody looks up a street number as a record in its own right — so `address` and `geo` are fields, siblings as they are on schema.org/Place, and either may be absent: a venue may be known only by its postal address, or a meeting point only by its coordinates. AT LEAST ONE OF THEM MUST BE PRESENT, because a Place with neither locates nothing. THIS RECORD IS NOT AN ACCESS CONTROL AND NOT A BOOKING. It says where somewhere is, and nothing about who may go there or whether it is free: capacity, equipment, rules and hourly price belong to a bookable room (eCommons' `Space`, 2d55b30d-2938-4bd5-99c5-04b090eec03a), which should point AT a Place rather than carry its own address. NO JOINING LINK GOES IN HERE: an online meeting's link is one attendee's access, not a property of a place, and the separation is copied from WVTTK, which declares `online` and `meetingLink` apart from `address` for exactly that reason.

placeId.description: Stable application id for this place, unchanged across edits. Distinct from the meta envelope id, which changes when the record is replaced.

name.description: What the place is called, as an invitation would name it — 'OBA Oosterdok', not 'Oosterdokskade 143'. schema.org `name`. This is the field a reader shows; it is required because a place nobody can name is of no use to anybody choosing where to go.

kind.description: What sort of place this is, as a lowercase word: library, hall, cafe, park, office, venue. Deliberately free text rather than an enum, because the useful vocabularies are external and much larger than anything worth freezing here: it maps to schema.org `additionalType` and to OpenStreetMap's primary tag value (`amenity=library`, `leisure=park`). A reader that does not recognise a value should ignore it rather than reject the record.

address.description: The postal address. Key names are taken unchanged from the only address shape in this ecosystem with live records behind it — the `address` block inside `Organization` (ad226473-640e-4d16-90e5-2fd96f261554), observed on 7 of its 19 records — so that an application reading one reads the other. Maps to schema.org `PostalAddress`: street→streetAddress, city→addressLocality, region→addressRegion, postalCode→postalCode, country→addressCountry. ONE DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FROM THAT SHAPE: `Organization` nests its coordinates inside this block, and here they are a sibling, because a Place may be a bare point with no address at all and coordinates wrapped in a key called `address` would be a lie. A reader bridging the two must look in both places.

street.description: Street name without the number. schema.org `streetAddress` combines the two; this ecosystem splits them, and the split is kept.

houseNumber.description: House or building number, as a string: '143', '143A', '143-145'.

postalCode.description: Postal or ZIP code, in the local format. schema.org `postalCode`.

region.description: State, province or region. schema.org `addressRegion`. Added here because `Organization`'s block has no field for it and many countries need one; a reader of that type will not expect it.

geo.description: Where this is on the ground. Key names and the two provenance fields are taken unchanged from `Organization.address.geo`, the only live coordinate shape in this ecosystem. Maps to schema.org `GeoCoordinates`: lat→latitude, lon→longitude. NOTE THE SPELLING: `lon`, not `lng`. Calendula declares `lng` in the inline `location` object on a CalendarEvent, and measured across 2000 CalendarEvent records not one of the 75 location objects carries a coordinate under either spelling — so there was nothing to stay compatible with, and the name that already has live data behind it wins.

source.description: Where the coordinates came from: `manual` when a person placed the pin, or the name of the service they were looked up in (`osm`, `google`). Recorded because a coordinate is a claim by whoever produced it, and a reader deciding whether to route somebody there is entitled to know who that was.

precision.description: How exact the coordinates are, in the vocabulary already in use on `Organization.address.geo`: `rooftop` for the building itself, through to coarser values for a street or a locality centroid. A door-level route built from a city-centre point is wrong in a way the number itself does not reveal.

updatedAt.description: When the coordinates were last established. Separate from the record's own `updatedAt` because a place can be renamed without being re-surveyed.

containedInPlace.description: The larger Place this one sits inside, as `w3ds://envelope?id=@<vault>/<metaEnvelopeId>` — a room inside a building, a building inside a campus. schema.org `containedInPlace`, and the reason this product has one place type rather than two: nesting is a reference to the same type, not a second type underneath. The pointer carries the vault as well as the envelope id because an envelope id alone addresses nothing; it is the form the registered `Relation` ontology (f9ff8527-f3af-4733-b8df-fa0c97ba03ff) documents for pointing at an envelope, and resolving it is the reader's business.

url.description: The place's own page on the web, if it has one. schema.org `url`.

photos.description: Pictures of the place. The `uri` form is the one eCommons' `Space` uses for the same purpose. Remember what that form means: the bytes behind a w3ds://file URI are served from a public host whatever the record's audience says, so nothing private goes here.

importedFrom.description: Where this record's contents came from, when they were looked up in a map service rather than typed. AN OBSERVATION BY THE PLATFORM THAT WROTE IT, never a claim by the place itself, and it must not be shown as though the place had asserted it. Present so that a stale import is recognisable as an import: a building renamed in OpenStreetMap last week does not change what we copied last year, and a reader can decide whether to re-check.

provider.description: `osm`, `google`, or `manual` when a person typed it.

externalId.description: That provider's own identifier, verbatim — an OSM element such as `way/34633854`, or a Google place id. Keeps a re-check possible without matching on name.

ownerEName.description: eName of the vault this record lives on — whoever described the place, not whoever owns the building. A Place is a description, and several descriptions of the same building may exist; `importedFrom.externalId` is what makes them recognisable as the same place.

createdAt.description: When this place was first described, by whoever described it.

updatedAt.description: When the description was last rewritten. A place does not move; this changes when somebody corrects the address, the name or the coordinates.
